Description: An adenocarcinoma cell line established by D.J. Giard in 1972 from lung carcinoma tissue removed from a 58-year-old Caucasian male.

A class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system - the largest and most numerous neuroglial cells in the brain and spinal cord. Astrocytes are irregularly shaped with many long processes, including those with 'end feet' which form the glial (limiting) membrane and directly and indirectly contribute to the blood-brain barrier. They regulate the extracellular ionic and chemical environment, and 'reactive astrocytes' (along with microglia) respond to injury.
A lymphocyte of B lineage that is capable of B cell mediated immunity.
Cells sorted or enriched for CD138 (syndecan-1) surface expression, typically plasma cells.
A T cell expressing an alpha-beta T cell receptor and the CD8 coreceptor.
A neuron that uses acetylcholine as a vesicular neurotransmitter.
Cultured Neuronal cells derived from Olfactory Neuroepithelium
Any hematopoietic stem cell that is part of a umbilical cord blood.
A CNS neuron of the forebrain.
Neuron generated by direct conversion (transdifferentiation) of somatic cells such as fibroblasts without passing through a pluripotent intermediate state, bypassing the need for iPSC generation
A neuron that releases dopamine as a neurotransmitter. Includes subtypes such as midbrain dopaminergic neurons.
A stem cell of embryonic origin.

An endothelial cell comprises the outermost layer or lining of anatomical structures and can be squamous or cuboidal. In mammals, endothelial cell has vimentin filaments and is derived from the mesoderm.

A cell that is usually found in a two-dimensional sheet with a free surface. The cell has a cytoskeleton that allows for tight cell to cell contact and for cell polarity where the apical part is directed towards the lumen and the basal part to the basal lamina.
In cell morphology, epithelial-like cells are polygonal in shape with more regular dimensions, and grow attached to a substrate in discrete patches.

A connective tissue cell which secretes an extracellular matrix rich in collagen and other macromolecules. Flattened and irregular in outline with branching processes; appear fusiform or spindle-shaped.
A neuron that uses GABA as a vesicular neurotransmitter.
The delicate network of branched cells and fibers that supports the tissue of the central nervous system.
A neuron that is capable of some neurotransmission by glutamate secretion.

A hematopoietic multipotent progenitor cell is multipotent, but not capable of long-term self-renewal. These cells are characterized as lacking lineage cell surface markers and being CD34-positive in both mice and humans.
Any hematopoietic cell that is a precursor of some other hematopoietic cell type.
A neuron with a soma found in the hippocampus.

A cell in the immune system that is involved in host defense. This category may include lymphocytes, monocytes, macrophages, neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils, mast cells, and thrombocytes. Precursor cells in these lineages may also be included.

Neuron produced by forced expression of neurogenic transcription factors (e.g. NGN2) in pluripotent stem cells, such as iPSC-derived induced neurons (iNeurons). For neurons made by direct conversion of somatic cells without a pluripotent intermediate, use directly-converted neurons instead.
Undifferentiated iPSC. Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPS cells or iPSCs) are a type of pluripotent stem cell artificially derived from a non-pluripotent cell.
Astrocytes derived from iPSCs.
Endothelial cells derived from iPSCs.
Glial cells derived from iPSCs.
Microglia and microglia-like cells derived from iPSCs.
Neurons derived from iPSCs
Neuronal-restricted progenitor cells derived from iPSCs, which differentiate only into neurons.
Pericytes derived from iPSCs.
A lymphocyte that has gotten larger after being stimulated by an antigen.
Human cell line from tissue infected with Epstein-Barr virus, resembling a lymphoblast.
A lymphocyte is a leukocyte commonly found in the blood and lymph that has the characteristics of a large nucleus, a neutral staining cytoplasm, and prominent heterochromatin.

A mononuclear phagocyte present in variety of tissues, typically differentiated from monocytes, capable of phagocytosing a variety of extracellular particulate material, including immune complexes, microorganisms, and dead cells.
An inhibitory, GABAergic projection neuron in the striatum that integrates glutamatergic signals arising from the cerebral cortex and thalamus.
A central nervous system cancer tissue that are manifested in the central nervous system and arise from the arachnoid 'cap' cells of the arachnoid villi in the meninges.

A transcriptomically distinct central nervous system macrophage found in the parenchyma of the central nervous system. Markers include CD11b-positive, F4/80-positive, and CD68-positive. Unlike macroglial cells, microglial cells arise from hematopoietic stem cells in the yolk sac during early embryogenesis that populate the central nervous system.
Myeloid mononuclear recirculating leukocyte that can act as a precursor of tissue macrophages, osteoclasts and some populations of tissue dendritic cells.
immune cells formed when blood monocytes enter the central nervous system and adapt a microglia-like state.
A mature contractile cell, commonly known as a myocyte. This cell has as part of its cytoplasm myofibrils organized in various patterns.
Neocortical neuroepithelial stem cells

Is a neuronal nuclear antigen that is commonly used as a biomarker for neurons and NeuN immunoreactivity has been widely used to identify neurons in tissue culture to measure the neuron(positive)/glia(negative) ratio in brain regions.

Is a neuronal nuclear antigen that is commonly used as a biomarker for neurons and NeuN immunoreactivity has been widely used to identify neurons in tissue culture to measure the neuron(positive)/glia(negative) ratio in brain regions.

A cell of the neural crest. Neural crest cells are multipotent. Premigratory neural crest cells are found at the neural plate boarder, some of which will undergo ectomesynchymal transition and delamination to form migratory neural crest cells.
The stem cell from which glial precursor cell arises from.

An undifferentiated cell derived from a neural stem cell, with a limited capacity to self-renew (Dibajnia and Morshead, 2013) and the ability to generate multiple types of lineage-restricted progenitors, contributing to the formation of neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes. Also referred to as neural precursor cell.

An undifferentiated neural cell that originates from the neuroectoderm and has the capacity both to perpetually self-renew without differentiating and to generate multiple central nervous system neuronal and glial cell types.

Malignant tumour cell derived from primitive ganglion cells. Mainly a tumour of childhood. Commonest sites are adrenal medulla and retroperitoneal tissue. The cells may partially differentiate into cells having the appearance of immature neurons.
The basic cellular unit of nervous tissue. Each neuron consists of a body, an axon, and dendrites. Their purpose is to receive, conduct, and transmit impulses in the nervous system.
A neuron that release noradrenaline (noriphinephrine) as a neurotransmitter.
A class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system. Form the insulating myelin sheath of axons in the central nervous system.

A proliferative and migratory glial progenitor cell that derives from a neural stem cell and resides within the central nervous system. It possesses the capacity to differentiate into a committed oligodendrocyte progenitor (COP) through a well-defined series of maturation steps, ultimately giving rise to a myelinating oligodendrocyte (MOL). In mice and humans, it is characterized by the expression of specific molecular markers, including Pdgfra, Cspg4 (also known as NG2) and Olig2.
A leukocyte with a single non-segmented nucleus in the mature form found in the circulatory pool of blood.

A pluripotent stem cell has the ability to form cells from all three germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm). However, unlike totipotent stem cells, they cell can not generate all the cells of the whole organism such as placenta.

A precursor cell that has a tendency to differentiate into a specific type of cell. They are descendants of stem cells, only they are more constrained in their differentiation potential or capacity for self-renewal, and are often more limited in both senses.

Nerve cells of the RETINA in the pathway of transmitting light signals to the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. They include the outer layer of PHOTORECEPTOR CELLS, the intermediate layer of RETINAL BIPOLAR CELLS and AMACRINE CELLS, and the internal layer of RETINAL GANGLION CELLS.
Schwann cells are a variety of glial cell that keep peripheral nerve fibres (both myelinated and unmyelinated) alive.

A glioblast cell that develops from a migratory neural crest cell. The SCP is embedded among neurons (axons) with minimal extracellular spaces separating them from nerve cell membranes and has no basal lamina. In rodents SCPs are the only cells in the Schwann cell lineage that expresses Cdh19.
A neoplasm that arises from SCHWANN CELLS of the cranial, peripheral, and autonomic nerves.
Human neuroblastoma clonal subline of the neuroepithelioma cell line SK-N-SH that had been established in 1970 from the bone marrow biopsy of a 4-year-old girl with metastatic neuroblastoma.
A motor neuron that passes from the spinal cord toward or to a muscle and conducts an impulse that causes movement.
Neuron found in the spiral ganglion.
